newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 8.5 trln lire BTP, CCTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 8.5 trln lire BTP, CCTs.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected on average to issue some 8.5 trillion lire of fixed-rate bonds (BTP) and floating-rate certificates (CCT) at its mid-month medium and long term paper auction, a Reuter poll of economists showed.

On November 15, the Treasury will hold an auction of a new first tranche of November 1, 2003 CCTs with a first coupon of 3.80 percent, and a third tranche of November 1, 2006 BTPs with a 7.75 percent coupon.
On November 18, October 1, 1999 BTPs with a 7.50 percent coupon and September 15, 2001 BTPs with a 7.75 percent coupon will be on offer.
The Treasury will announce the amounts of the four issues on Tuesday, November 12.

"The Treasury is likely to continue its policy of limited issues, but I expect fair volume for the CCT in order to give liquidity for a new instrument," said Davide Tesoro of Banque Indosuez in Milan.

Roberta Costantini of Banca di Roma, however, said the CCT issue could in fact be fairly modest given a certain lack of public interest in this paper and given that the Treasury's policy for some time now has been to transfer part of its medium to long-term debt from CCTs to BTPs.
